description: We are a Guadalajara-based team interested in data, AI, health  and Earth science. We are looking for people with skills in coding, data visualization, or communication who want to build a solution with real impact. I bring experience in web development and technology consulting, and a human-centered perspective on solution design.

details:
Delta-Me is a crew health console for astronauts who are far from a doctor. On the way to Mars, a question to Earth and its answer can take up to 40 minutes, so the crew has to notice health changes and act on them by themselves. Lab reports don't help much: their "normal ranges" describe people living on Earth, not the astronaut holding the report. Delta-Me gives every crew member a digital avatar that stores their own pre-flight baseline, and asks a sharper question: is this normal for you?

WHAT IT DOES

- Personal baselines: every new blood result is compared with that astronaut's own pre-flight draws as well as the Earth lab range. Each body system lights up on a clickable 3D avatar as Nominal, Caution or Warning, with plain-language explanations.

- Confirm, then act: one odd value is often chance (about 3% with three baseline draws), so it asks for a repeat test (Caution). It becomes a Warning only when the whole crew shifts together or a repeat draw confirms it; a value outside the lab range is a Warning at once. Every alert says what to do now and how long Earth will take to reply from where the crew is.

- Radiation: the console replays the real ISS dosimeter record of the September 2017 solar storm. A simple onboard rule stayed quiet from 4 to 10 September, then fired a storm-shelter Warning at 05:52 UTC on 11 September. A live mode follows NOAA's GOES proton feed.

- Self-assessment between blood tests: a daily check-in (sleep, mood, blood pressure, glucose, temperature), a camera pulse reading, and a readiness model trained on NASA's Crew State Monitoring data.

- Mission worlds: ISS, Mars transit, Moon and a Mars base, with guidance for each environment. Each astronaut can create a photo avatar on their own device (pose detection plus per-part Gaussian splats), with anatomical organs placed on their own body. A guided use case and an interface walkthrough explain every part of the screen.

WHAT WE FOUND IN REAL NASA DATA

We tested the idea on the Inspiration4 blood panels in NASA's Open Science Data Repository (OSD-569, OSD-575). The day after landing, the lab ranges called every crew member's red-cell size (MCV) normal: 87.0 to 90.5 fL, inside 80 to 100. Against each person's own baseline, MCV had fallen in all four, by 3.44 standard deviations on average. At the later draws, none of 88 crew-wide checks reached 3 SD (the largest was 2.70). Four people on one 3-day flight make this a hypothesis worth flying, not proof that the flight caused it, and we say so in the app.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Catch changes that population ranges hide, before they become problems; avoid false alarms by confirming before acting; give actions that account for the communication delay. It supports Earth-independent medical operations for Artemis and future Mars crews, and the same personal-baseline idea helps remote and polar teams on Earth.

TOOLS

React 19, TypeScript, Vite, three.js with React Three Fiber, MediaPipe Pose (in the browser), Recharts, Remotion; Python for the data pipeline and statistics, matplotlib for figures; hosted on Netlify. No backend and no accounts: photos and check-ins stay on the device. 3D models from NASA 3D Resources; organ meshes from the HuBMAP 3D Reference Object Library. Live demo: https://delta-me-astronaut-health.netlify.app

WHY IT IS CREATIVE

It replaces "normal for people on Earth" with "normal for you", adds an honest confirmation step instead of alarming on every outlier, makes escalation aware of distance from Earth, and shows each astronaut as an avatar of their own baseline inside the mission world.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Honest statistics (small sample, chance rate, what the data cannot prove), privacy (anonymized crew C001 to C004, on-device photos), a clear interface (icons plus text, never color alone; works on phones), and safety (decision support for training, not a medical device). Super Intelligence use is disclosed in the README and in the video.

Team Órbita Tapatía: Diego Romero and Ernesto Ramirez.
